newsitem.title: UK: Euro fuel barges steady, Med cargo trades high.
newsitem.headline: Euro fuel barges steady, Med cargo trades high.

text.p: NWE fuel markets were slow moving on Wednesday, though demand from the western Mediterranean was helping to ease a potential overhang of cracked Russian cargoes, traders said.

High sulphur barges were dull though prices were stable, with prompt delivery trades of $90 and $92 a tonne in Antwerp. Swaps firmed 75 cents and Rotterdam sellers were quoted as sticking at $92 and above.
Some 20,000 tonnes of Russian cracked M100 was traded to the Canary Islands for bunker fuel on Tuesday at $99 cif a tonne. Other offers to the buyer were around high cif plus $4 or $5.

The high price was said to reflect the lack of good quality Russian material from the Black Sea and the buyer complained that further purchases were being made difficult by quality problems with the Baltic barrels on offer.
